question: Does leakage-safe labeled target-subject calibration improve the validated four-class full-covariance hierarchy, and which pair branch should be calibrated?

protocol.outer_validation: 30 repeated subject folds from seeds 11, 23, 37, 51, and 71
protocol.source_model: saved nested-selected offset_3_length_8 hierarchy configurations; feature ranking, covariance, coarse gate, and hierarchy weight use source subjects only
protocol.target_calibration: one to five labeled runs from the held-out subject; the evaluation run is always excluded
protocol.alpha_selection: leave-one-calibration-run-out pair accuracy; evaluation-run labels are never used

calibration_only_gate_followup.diagnostic: leave-one-calibration-run-out arm gain before evaluating the held-out run
calibration_only_gate_followup.conclusion: Calibration-run internal gain does not predict held-out benefit. The fixed gate discards a significant part of the universal gain, while the cross-subject threshold converges to applying calibration almost universally. Close this simple gating lane.

conclusion: Labeled target-subject calibration is a real full-model improvement when restricted to the weaker arm branch and supplied at least three runs. Four to five runs give robust all-subject and QC-stratified gains. One run is harmful, two are inconclusive, and leg calibration adds no value. Keep 0.8752 as the zero-label benchmark and 0.8913 as the five-run labeled-personalization result. A calibration-only internal-gain gate was tested and failed to identify regressions; universal light arm calibration remains the best validated labeled policy once at least three runs are available.
